subject: Burst capacity & queueing policy for Dedicated GPUs - ACME
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <ops@acme-industries.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme-industries.com
Date: Sat, 13 Jun 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool — recurring queueing during nightly batch windows

Connor —

We're seeing a recurring backlog on our Dedicated pool between 02:00–04:00 UTC over the past three nights. Latency spikes and token-per-second throughput drops even though we have 8 reserved GPUs on the pool. We've attached the logs and a small sample CSV with per-minute queue depth and p95/p99 latency numbers.

Key facts from our end:
- Nightly batch runs: 01:50–03:55 UTC, bursts of short-lived high-concurrency jobs (~600 concurrent requests for ~30s bursts).
- Observed queue depth peaks: up to 240 requests queued.
- Observed p99 latency: ~1.2s during spikes, p95 around 550ms.
- Throughput drop: token/sec down ~40% vs steady-state.

Expectation from the contract: guaranteed sustained throughput for the reserved GPUs and defined queueing behavior so our SLAs to our internal customers hold. Can Redwood confirm if we're hitting a scheduling limit or if queueing policy is deprioritizing these short bursts? We urgently need either a technical mitigation (pre-warm/burst pool) or a temporary SLA amendment for these nightly windows.

Thanks,
Jordan Ellis
Principal SRE — Acme Industries
attachments: acme_nightly_spike_logs.csv
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <ops@acme-industries.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 08:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool — recurring queueing during nightly batch windows

Jordan — thanks for the log bundle and the clear summary. Looping in Aditya (runtime) and Lauren (account lead) so we can triage and propose options.

Short answer: there are two plausible causes — (1) continuous batching + KV cache warmup that favors steady request flows, and (2) autoscaler cooldown/queue-threshold logic that avoids spinning new worker nodes for very short spikes. We can address this with either a configuration change (burst credits / pre-warm policy) or an SLA addendum that grants you guaranteed burst headroom during your nightly window.

Next steps I propose:
- Aditya: can you review the logs and confirm whether the queueing is due to batching/kv-cache behavior or autoscale delays?
- Jordan: can you confirm how exact the window is night-to-night (fixed 01:50–03:55 UTC)? If it's variable, what's the max expected duration of an individual burst?
- Lauren: I'll prepare a draft addendum outlining a 2-hour guaranteed burst allotment (2x reserved GPUs capacity for 2 hours daily) and an operational playbook — will flag pricing and approval items.

Connor
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Jordan Ellis <ops@acme-industries.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool — recurring queueing during nightly batch windows

Jordan / team — I dug into the CSV and trace headers. Notes: 
- The request pattern is bursty with many short-lived sessions (avg token sequence length small, high QPS). Our continuous batching logic increases latency for very short bursts because it tries to build batches up to a per-GPU token budget before dispatch, and KV cache misses on first requests add ~70-120ms per instance during warmup.
- Autoscaler is configured with a 90s cooldown and a threshold of sustained queue depth > 100 for scale-up; since your bursts are often 30–45s, the autoscaler often doesn't react.

Mitigations we can implement quickly (48–72 hours):
1) Temporary pre-warm policy for your pool during 01:40–04:00 UTC that keeps an extra 2 nodes hot (reduces queueing and KV-warm cost).
2) Shorten autoscaler cooldown to 30s for this pool and lower the scale-up queue threshold to 50 (will increase churn slightly).
3) Enable burst credits: we can allow temporary overcommit to 2x reserved GPUs for up to 2 hours/day; usage beyond that will be billed at burst rates.

All three are technically feasible. If you need formal guarantees on uptime/latency for that window, we'll need a short SLA addendum to lock in the burst allotment and commit to rollback safeguards. Connor / Lauren, any constraints from commercial/legal on a temporary addendum?

— Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <ops@acme-industries.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 13:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool — recurring queueing during nightly batch windows

Jordan — appreciate the detail and Aditya's quick analysis. Commercial note: we can offer a scoped SLA addendum that guarantees an agreed burst profile for a defined daily window. Preliminary commercial terms:
- Guaranteed burst: +2 GPU-equivalent capacity for up to 2 hours/day between 01:40–04:00 UTC.
- Price: additional monthly charge (flat) plus per-token burst overage at standard burst rate.
- Rollout: 7-day tech validation, then a 30-day pilot with monitoring dashboards and weekly checkpoints.
- Exit: customers can revert to baseline reserved pool config with 72-hour notice.

I'll prepare a short addendum PDF and a DocuSign envelope. Connor: please confirm the pricing band we discussed in pipeline (I have the draft reflecting the mid-tier burst rate). Jordan: if that window is firm, we can start the validation next week and aim to have the pilot in place within 10 business days.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_proposed_sla_addendum_v1.pdf
From: Jordan Ellis <ops@acme-industries.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool — recurring queueing during nightly batch windows

Thanks — that approach sounds workable. Confirmations: 
- Nightly window: typically 01:50–03:55 UTC; can shift by +/- 10 minutes, but individual bursts remain 20–60s in length.
- We accept a 2-hour daily burst allotment and the 7-day validation. Please include language in the addendum about: (1) monitoring coverage (we need access to a read-only observability link and token-level cost breakdown during the pilot), (2) rollback safety (no automatic draining of our pool during validation), and (3) a p99 target of <=800ms for the burst window (we understand steady-state guarantees may be different).

I'll sign the DocuSign once I review the addendum. Appreciate the fast response — Aditya / Connor / Lauren, let's sync on the kickoff for validation early next week.

Jordan
Principal SRE — Acme Industries
